components.css: .ds-nav { position: fixed; top: 0; left: 0; right: 0; z-index: 100; background: rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.6); backdrop-filter: blur(24px); -webkit-backdrop-filter: blur(24px); border-bottom: 1px solid oklch(1 0 0 / 10%); transition: all 500ms ease-out; } .ds-nav-inner { display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; padding: 1rem; max-width: 1280px; margin: 0 auto; } .ds-logo { font-size: 1.5rem; font-weight: 700; color: #ffffff; text-decoration: none; letter-spacing: -0.05em; font-family: Geist, system-ui, sans-serif; } .ds-logo-dot { color: oklch(0.585 0.233 277.117); } .ds-nav-right { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 1.5rem; } .ds-status-pill { display: none; align-items: center; gap: 0.5rem; padding: 4px 12px; border-radius: 9999px; background: oklch(0.14 0 0 / 50%); border: 1px solid #27272a; } @media (min-width: 1024px) { .ds-status-pill { display: flex; } } .ds-ping-dot { width: 8px; height: 8px; position: relative; display: inline-flex; } .ds-ping-dot::before { content: ''; position: absolute; width: 100%; height: 100%; border-radius: 50%; background: oklch(0.585 0.233 277.117); animation: ping 1s cubic-bezier(0, 0, 0.2, 1) infinite; opacity: 0.75; } .ds-ping-dot::after { content: ''; width: 8px; height: 8px; border-radius: 50%; background: oklch(0.585 0.233 277.117); position: relative; } @keyframes ping { 75%, 100% { transform: scale(2); opacity: 0; } } .ds-status-text { font-family: Geist Mono, monospace; font-size: 0.625rem; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.2em; color: oklch(0.63 0 0); } .ds-menu-btn { padding: 8px; background: transparent; border: none; border-radius: 12px; cursor: pointer; transition: all 200ms ease-out; } .ds-menu-btn:hover { background: oklch(0.14 0 0); } .ds-menu-btn:active { transform: scale(0.9); }

narrative.overview: Precision, focus, and deliberate exposure. Like a photographer in a darkroom developing a print — every chemical decision matters, nothing is accidental. The interface is a clean, dark canvas where light (the indigo accent) appears only where it's needed to guide the eye. The system trusts that engineering minds appreciate restraint: fewer elements, higher signal. This is the opposite of the standard developer portfolio — no particles, no neon, no 'Hello World'. The surface communicates skill through quality of execution, not through decoration.
keyCharacteristics: Dark-first, indigo-lit: a near-black canvas where indigo acts as a precision tool — sparing, intentional, and always meaningful
Flat-by-default, tonal layering: depth comes from shifts in value (zinc-800 → zinc-900 → black), never from box-shadows
Monospaced labels as structural metadata: uppercase tracked mono text labels serve as a consistent system annotation layer
Motion enhances hierarchy: entrances are staggered, transitions are deliberate — never gratuitous, never animated for its own sake

rules.name: The Rare Color Rule
rules.body: The indigo accent appears on no more than ~10% of any given screen. Its scarcity is what makes it meaningful.

rules.name: The Neutral Discipline Rule
rules.body: Every neutral is a true neutral (chroma 0). No warm or cool tinting.

rules.name: The One Family Rule
rules.body: No second display font. If text needs distinction, use weight, size, or mono.

rules.name: The Label Ceiling Rule
rules.body: Labels never exceed 0.75rem. They are annotation, not content.

rules.name: The Flat Rest Rule
rules.body: At rest, every surface is flat. Box-shadows do not exist. Depth is read through background color shifts.

dos: Do use indigo sparingly — its rarity is its power
Do layer surfaces by value (darker → lighter) for depth instead of shadows
Do use Geist Mono for labels, code references, and metadata
Do stagger entrance animations with 0.2s delays for deliberate reveals
Do keep body text at text-zinc-400 or lighter against the dark canvas
Do use semantic HTML — nav, main, section, proper heading hierarchy
Do respect prefers-reduced-motion — every animation needs a reduced alternative
donts: Don't use gradient text (bg-clip-text text-transparent) — use a single solid color for emphasis via weight or size
Don't put an uppercase tracked eyebrow label above every section — use at most one per page, or none
Don't use box-shadows — tonal layering is the elevation system
Don't use numbered section markers (01 / 02 / 03) unless the content is literally sequential
Don't use z-index values outside the semantic scale (50, 100, 105, 110, 120, 130) — never 999, 9999
Don't use side-stripe borders (border-left > 1px) as accent — use full borders or background tint instead
Don't animate layout properties — stick to opacity, transform, and filter
Don't use standard dev portfolio clichés — no particles, no neon, no 'Hello World', no stock illustrations
Don't leave commented-out code blocks in production files
Don't use invalid HTML attributes as props on Link/Button components
